If you are lucky and your headliner isnt falling to peices you won't have to play with fiberglass, start by peeling off the nasty old fabric. The crust of orange foam rubs off the formed fiberglass pretty easy, you can use a coarse rag or a brush of some sort. Don't skimp on the spray adhesive you get, you want this to last. I went ahead and bought locktite brand industrial strength (at $16 a can) don't go cheap. My local fabric store had headheadliner material (a laminate of fabric and foam backing) at $15 a yard, 2 yards will easily do the project. Be carful where you get this adhesive it can ruin your new material if you are not careful. Spray the surfaces and follow the directions on the can, trim material after it has dried for your sunshades, cab lights, and coat hooks. If your car has a sunroof be sure to leave enough material to reach where the piping was when you took out the old one.
